senses: A dish consisting of layers of minced lamb or beef, sliced aubergine (eggplant) or potatoes, tomatoes and béchamel sauce, baked in the oven.
ety: Borrowed from Greek μουσακάς (mousakás), from Ottoman Turkish موصاقه (musakka), from Arabic مُسَقَّعَة (musaqqaʕa) or originally from Arabic مُصَقَّعَة (muṣaqqaʕa), from the trilateral root ص ق ع (ṣ q ʕ): “to hit, to pound, to smash”.

senses: One who is being protected.
One who is under official protection.
A person in the business of devising, writing, illustrating or selling advertisements.
A native or inhabitant of the east of a region (or of the world as a whole), such as one of the eastern United States.
A large grey crane (Antigone rubicunda, syn. Grus rubicunda), of northern and eastern Australia.
examples: We wade through the delicate water, the moon spilling on our colourless bodies. Brolgas ruffling their wings against water ribbons, making the muddy bath flinch in coiling waves.

senses: One who takes part in the sport of karting.
Dull, dreary; melancholy.
ety: From Scots dowie, apparently a form of dull + -ly.
examples: There was no comfort in the goodliness of spring or the bright sunshine weather, and she who had been wont to go about the doors lightfoot and blithe was now as dowie as a widow woman.

senses: A captain or skipper of a boat.
A putter: one who puts the tubs of coal from the workings to the cranes, flats, or stations, so that they can be conveyed to the surface.
A street vendor selling fruit and vegetables from a barrow.
ety: From barrow + -man. Prior to the introduction of underground tramways, coal was carried on barrows.

senses: A woman with offspring.
A broad, shallow concavity, notably of a bone.
ety: Borrowing from Latin venter (“the belly; the womb; a swelling”).

senses: Shaped like an olive
The act of adjusting one's dress or appearance; the act of sprucing oneself up.
ety: Perhaps alteration (due to primp) of prank (“to deck, adorn”), from Middle English pranken (“to trim”), or from Middle Dutch prinken (“to deck for show, parade in fine apparel”) (from pronk (“show, display”) or from Middle Low German prunken (from prank (“display”)). Cognate with Middle Dutch pronken (“to flaunt”), German Prunk (“a show, parade, splendour”), Danish and Swedish prunk.

senses: Of a gem or precious stone: of inferior value or quality.
ety: Borrowed from Middle French occidental, from Latin occidentalis, equivalent to occident + -al.

senses: Towards the upper part of a field.
Synonym of English.
The third letter of the several Semitic alphabets (Phoenician, Aramaic, Hebrew, Syriac).
ety: From Hebrew גימל (gimel); ultimately from Proto-Semitic word for a weapon which was debatably either a staff sling or a throwing stick. Doublet of gamma.

senses: Growing well under salty conditions
examples: We planted a halophytic species of grass.

senses: Someone who transgresses.
ety: From Middle English transgressour, from Anglo-Norman transgressour, from Latin transgressor. Equivalent to transgress + -or.

senses: The act or process of deconflicting.
An action movie.
A tree, Adansonia digitata, native to tropical Africa, having a broad swollen trunk and edible gourd-like hanging fruits.
ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin bahobab, from Arabic أَبُو حِبَاب (ʔabū ḥibāb, “father of many seeds”), from أَبُو (ʔabū, “father”) + حَبّ (ḥabb, “seed”).

senses: The concentration of a substance as determined by titration.
ety: From French titre. Doublet of tilde, title, titlo, tittle, and titulus.

senses: A shrub inhabiting western North America (Amelanchier alnifolia).
The edible berry of this shrub.
ety: From Cree ᒥᓵᐢᑿᑑᒥᐣ (misaaskwatoomin, “saskatoon berry”), from ᒥᓵᐢᑿᐟ (misaaskwat, “saskatoon shrub”) + ᒥᐣ (min, “berry”).

senses: A sweetened thick drink or thin gruel made from cornmeal, served hot.
ety: From Spanish atole, from Classical Nahuatl ātōlli.
examples: Since the days of the Tarascans, the corn-loving folks of Michoacan have enjoyed atole, a maize-based gruel flavored with chocolate, fruit, tamarind, or herbs.
Visitors can learn to make their own tortillas or sample the traditional cornmeal drink atole.

senses: Marked or numbered with a barcode.
A high short punt onto or behind the defending team.
ety: After the Irish Garryowen Football Club, named from Garryowen, Limerick.

senses: Like a dwarf; being especially small or stunted.
examples: The vegetation, as might be supposed, is scant, or at least dwarfish.
There were the Rougiers, for instance, an old, ragged, dwarfish couple who plied an extraordinary trade.

senses: To make a sound
Having flight feathers (for example, upon reaching maturity).
Capable of flight.
Having a specified number or kind of flights (of stairs, a screw thread, etc.).
The identity and nature of one's parents, and in particular, the legitimacy of one's birth.
The social quality of one's class in society.
Origin; derivation.
ety: From Middle French, from Old French parentage.
examples: English gentlemen, after all, do not discriminate against each other on the grounds of parentage, only of breeding.
Annabel was, like the writer, of mixed parentage: half-English, half-Dutch, in her case. I remember her features far less distinctly today than I did a few years ago, before I knew Lolita.
My fortunes parentage — good parentage — To equal mine! — was it not thus? What say you?

senses: The process or act of deselecting.
A fermented fish sauce popular as a condiment in Ancient Rome.
ety: From Latin garum, from Ancient Greek γάρον (gáron, “the fish whose intestines were originally used in the condiment's production”).

senses: Having a pigtail.
examples: Old pigtailed seamen would tell of horseshoes found in the meat casks; of curious barkings and neighings heard in the slaughter-houses; and of negroes who disappeared near the victualling yards, to be seen no more.

senses: A tribal conference held by Nguni leaders.
Any conference, discussion, or meeting.
Chiefly in one's own or someone's indaba: a concern, matter, or problem.
An international conference of Scout leaders.
ety: Borrowed from Zulu índaba (“affair, issue, matter; piece of news; story”), from ín- (class 9 noun prefix) + -daɓa (stem meaning ‘affair, matter’).

senses: A graphical representation, using polar coordinates, of the interactions of a central entity
A very compact car.
examples: GM announced plans to sell a tiny "microcar" called the Chevrolet Beat in Europe next year.

senses: The process of becoming, or the state of being, acclimated, or habituated to a new climate, surroundings, or situation; especially, acclimatization.
An electronic device or software that alters the sound of an instrument by combining out-of-phase copies of its original sound.
A mechanical device used to remove ice and snow from railway lines.
One who makes wisecracks, particularly in a sassy or cocky fashion.
A thick paste made from yam or cassava flour, eaten chiefly in Yoruba cuisine.
examples: The amala, or fermented yam, is an acquired taste, arriving in a grayish steamed mound, wrapped in plastic; it's neither sweet nor sour.
